question: Can the Qwen3-14B Full verifier run on a 48 GB GPU by keeping the weights in bf16 in GPU memory while every operation still computes in fp32, and does it reach the same verdicts as the 80 GB verifier?
method: A research patch (off unless NOET_REPLAY_WEIGHTS=bf16) keeps linear and embedding weights in bf16 and widens them to fp32 at each call; bf16 to fp32 is exact, so each layer sees the same fp32 values as a model loaded in fp32. First, Qwen3-0.6B logits were compared between an fp32 load and the patch. Then 23 recorded Qwen3-14B Full verification requests (heights 8 to 61 of a recorded test set; 20 GREEN and 3 RED by the 80 GB verifier) were verified again on one GPU with the recorded replay seed, one after another in a single process.

replay.failure: needs ~29306MB but no GPU has room after eviction
replay.failurePattern: strictly alternating: every request after a completed one failed (about 165 s), the next one completed (about 300 s)

findings: bf16 weight storage with fp32 compute gave bit-identical Qwen3-0.6B logits (maximum difference 0.0).
Every Qwen3-14B request that ran reached the verdict the 80 GB verifier recorded: 10 GREEN and 2 RED.
Peak GPU memory in use was 45,692 MiB (about 44.6 GiB) of the card's 49,140 MiB, against about 70 GiB for the fp32 replay.
11 of 23 requests could not run: the model cache does not free the previous request's memory before loading again, so every second request fails.
notEstablished: That the alternating eviction failure can be fixed; until it is, half of all blocks would get no verdict.
Bit-identical Qwen3-14B logits against an fp32 load (exactness was measured on Qwen3-0.6B only).
The third recorded RED request: it fell on a failed run and was not replayed.
Long-running operation as the live verifier, with the relays, on mainnet.
Headroom under longer prompts or outputs than the 23 recorded requests (peak reserved memory was 44.3 GiB of 48).
Other 48 GB cards (A40, L40S) and community hosts.
evidence: Pod output (exactness.json, replay-bf16.jsonl, replay-bf16/summary.json and failure reports, gpu-memory-test.csv) is kept privately with the session records.
